verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization server that covers most of what an MCP authorization flow relies on. It has a well-known discovery endpoint, a dynamic client registration endpoint, token introspection for validating access tokens, token revocation, client-credentials and device grants for non-browser agents, and fine-grained authorization services for scoping access. Nothing in the evidence ties this to MCP specifically, and several pieces the MCP auth spec depends on are not shown. missing for 10: explicit MCP authorization-spec compliance or guidance, protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) and resource indicators/audience binding, documented PKCE support for public agent clients, explicit OAuth scope configuration, independent or hands-on corroboration of Keycloak fronting an MCP server.
